resteasy_liberty_workflow.mode_overview: This mode provides expert guidance for working with RESTeasy, Open Liberty, Jakarta EE, and MicroProfile codebases. It combines deep framework knowledge with practical implementation patterns to help analyze, debug, and enhance enterprise Java applications.

step.details: Identify the specific area of work: - RESTeasy integration (JAX-RS providers, filters, interceptors) - Open Liberty features (OSGi bundles, feature manifests) - Jakarta EE components (Servlets, CDI beans, EJBs, JPA entities) - MicroProfile implementations (Config, Metrics, Health, OpenAPI, etc.) - Cross-framework integration issues

tools.tool: search_files - Find related implementations across the codebase
list_code_definition_names - Understand class structures and relationships
read_file - Examine specific implementations in detail

focus_areas.area: Bundle activators and OSGi service registration

step.details: Understand how components interact: - How RESTeasy integrates with Liberty's servlet container - CDI bean discovery and injection mechanisms - OSGi service dependencies and lifecycle - Feature enablement and class loading - Configuration property resolution

steps.step: Use search_files to find relevant classes and patterns
Read feature manifests to understand dependencies
Examine OSGi bundle metadata (MANIFEST.MF, bnd.bnd)
Review CDI extension implementations
Check JAX-RS application and provider configurations
Trace request flow through filters and interceptors
Analyze CDI bean lifecycle and scopes
Review OSGi service registration and consumption
Examine exception handling and error responses
Check thread safety and concurrency patterns
Explain architectural patterns and design decisions
Identify potential issues or improvements
Provide framework-specific best practices
Suggest optimization opportunities
Identify affected components and dependencies
Determine required OSGi imports and exports
Plan CDI integration points
Design JAX-RS resource structure
Consider backward compatibility

phase.name: implementation
phase.description: Write or modify code following framework patterns

steps.step: Implement OSGi bundle activators if needed
Create or modify CDI beans with proper scopes
Implement JAX-RS resources, providers, or filters
Add MicroProfile annotations as appropriate
Update feature manifests and dependencies
Add proper logging and error handling

phase.name: integration
phase.description: Ensure proper integration with existing code

steps.step: Verify OSGi service wiring
Test CDI injection points
Validate JAX-RS endpoint registration
Check configuration property resolution
Ensure proper class loading and visibility
Review for framework-specific best practices
Check for common pitfalls (classloader issues, CDI scope problems)
Verify thread safety and resource management
Ensure proper error handling and logging
Validate against Jakarta EE/MicroProfile specifications

phase.name: problem_identification
phase.description: Understand the issue and its symptoms

steps.step: Gather error messages and stack traces
Identify which framework layer is involved
Check server logs for relevant messages
Review recent changes that might be related

phase.name: root_cause_analysis
phase.description: Trace the issue to its source

common_issues.issue: ClassNotFoundException or NoClassDefFoundError - Check OSGi imports/exports
CDI deployment errors - Verify bean discovery and injection points
JAX-RS endpoint not found - Check application path and resource registration
Configuration not applied - Verify property sources and precedence
Service not available - Check OSGi service lifecycle and dependencies

steps.step: Examine relevant bundle manifests and feature definitions
Check CDI bean archives and extensions
Review JAX-RS application configuration
Verify service component declarations
Trace through framework initialization code

phase.name: resolution
phase.description: Fix the issue and verify the solution

steps.step: Apply targeted fixes based on root cause
Update dependencies or configurations as needed
Add defensive code or validation where appropriate
Improve error messages for future debugging
Document the issue and solution

areas_to_check.area: CDI bean creation and injection costs

techniques.technique: Cache frequently accessed services or configurations
Use appropriate CDI scopes to minimize bean creation

steps.step: Measure performance impact
Ensure thread safety is maintained
Verify no regressions in functionality
Check resource usage (memory, threads)

workflow.description: Managing RESTEasy overlay files - files copied from upstream RESTEasy that Liberty needs to modify for integration purposes.
workflow.reference: See 5_overlay_file_workflow.xml for detailed instructions on: - Identifying RESTEasy versions from bnd.bnd files - Locating files in the RESTEasy repository - Finding commit hashes for specific versions - Creating overlay files with proper attribution - Maintaining source tracking comments
workflow.when_to_use: Use the overlay file workflow when you need to: - Add a new file from RESTEasy to a Liberty bundle - Update an existing overlay file to a newer RESTEasy version - Track the source of Liberty's RESTEasy modifications

completion_criteria.criterion: Code follows Jakarta EE and MicroProfile specifications
OSGi bundle metadata is correct and complete
JAX-RS resources are correctly registered and accessible
Error handling and logging are comprehensive
Thread safety and resource management are sound
Changes are compatible with existing Liberty features

key_principles.principle: Understand the OSGi lifecycle and service dynamics
Respect CDI bean scopes and injection points
Follow JAX-RS provider and filter ordering rules
Implement proper error handling at framework boundaries
Maintain backward compatibility with existing features
